# Input Validation, Output Encoding and Injection (INP)

All data from outside the trust boundary is untrusted: user input, API responses, files, deep links, QR codes, SAP responses and data from other systems. Validate it where it enters, and use the safe API at the point where it is used (the "sink").

## SCS-INP-01 Validate all input on the server; client validation is for usability only

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: All input MUST be validated on the server against an allow-list of type, length, range, format and permitted values before it is used. Client-side validation MUST also be done for usability, but it is never relied on for security.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Prefer allow-lists (permitted values, patterns) over deny-lists.
- Validate the whole object: reject unknown fields and enforce business rules (for example quantity > 0, date not in the past).

Implementation (Flutter):

- Use Form/TextFormField validators on every input field: required, length, format and type.
- Validate data from deep links, QR codes, push payloads and API responses before use (for example int.tryParse, enum mapping).

Verification: Code review confirms every endpoint has server-side validation. Negative tests send oversized, malformed and unexpected values and expect HTTP 400.

## SCS-INP-02 Parameterize every database query

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every database operation MUST use parameterized queries or an ORM. User-supplied data MUST NEVER be concatenated or interpolated into SQL text. Table, column and sort names that come from input MUST be mapped through an allow-list.

Implementation (Flutter):

- sqflite: use where: "status = ?" with whereArgs. Never interpolate $value into rawQuery, where:, execute or drift customSelect.
- Escape % and _ in LIKE patterns built from user input.

Verification: Code review and SAST rule for SQL injection (for example Sonar S3649). Grep for FromSqlRaw, ExecuteSqlRaw, CommandText and rawQuery with string interpolation.

## SCS-INP-03 Encode output for its context to prevent XSS

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Output shown in web pages, WebViews or other interpreters MUST be encoded for its context using the framework's built-in encoding. Raw HTML from user input MUST NEVER be rendered. Built-in encoding MUST NOT be disabled.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Display untrusted text with Text widgets, which never interpret HTML.
- Never pass untrusted HTML to WebView loadHtmlString or to HTML-rendering widgets. If rich text is a real requirement, sanitize it on the server with a maintained sanitizer.
- Flutter web: never use package:web innerHTML (it is raw); use textContent.

Verification: Code review greps for Html.Raw, MarkupString, loadHtmlString and innerHTML. DAST / manual XSS test of every field that is shown back to users.

## SCS-INP-04 Build URLs, paths and commands with safe APIs

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: URLs, file paths and operating system commands MUST NOT be built by concatenating user input. Use the platform's URL builders with encoding, resolve and check file paths against a base folder, and pass command arguments as a list without a shell.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Build URLs with Uri(scheme:, host:, path:, queryParameters:) or Uri.https(), which encode values. Never concatenate input into a URL string.
- Before launchUrl, check the scheme and host against an allow-list.
- Sanitize file names (Path.basename) and keep files inside app-private directories.

Verification: Code review greps for Path.Combine with request data, Process.Start, Redirect(, launchUrl and string-built URIs.
